newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Meridor may cut civil-service hiring.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Meridor may cut civil-service hiring.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor is considering hiring fewer civil servants as a way of achieving further budget cuts next year, the finance ministry said on Thursday.

The ministry said that in a pre-recorded television interview to be broadcast later on Thursday, Meridor said the Treasury had still not determined where it would make the approximately two billion shekels in new spending cuts to be submitted to parliament next month.

Among the proposals being weighed, he said, was to reduce the hiring of new civil servants. He stressed, however, that there would be no layoffs. Meridor said Treasury officials were also considering reducing the ministries' procurement budgets.
He warned that if parliament did not approve the Treasury's 1997 budget, unemployment would rise.

Meridor faces strong opposition in parliament against the budget, which originally called for 4.9 billion shekels in cuts. Earlier this week, Meridor said he would seek an additional two billion shekels in reductions.
